f.title: Apply the definitions of overdose, off-label use, misuse and abuse, using clinical judgement for overdose
f.statement: For reports of special situations, the following definitions apply (VI.B.6.3 requires them to be applied): overdose is the administration of a quantity of a medicinal product, per administration or cumulatively, above the maximum recommended dose according to the authorised product information, and clinical judgement should always be applied; off-label use is the intentional use for a medical purpose not in accordance with the terms of the marketing authorisation; misuse is the intentional and inappropriate use not in accordance with the terms of the marketing authorisation; abuse is the persistent or sporadic, intentional excessive use of a medicinal product accompanied by harmful physical or psychological effects (DIR Art 1(16)).

rows.quote: Where the primary source reports a suspect or interacting branded/proprietary medicinal product name without indicating the pharmaceutical form/presentation of the product and where the proprietary/branded medicinal product can be one of two or more possible pharmaceutical forms/presentations, which have different compositions in a country, the ICSR should be populated as follows in line with ICH-E2B: Reference E2B(R2)/(R3) requirements ICH-E2B(R2)  Data element B.4.k.2.1'Proprietary medicinal product name' should be populated with the proprietary/branded medicinal product name as reported by the primary source.  Data element B.4.k.2.2 'Active substance name(s)' should be completed with those active substances, which are in common to all pharmaceutical forms/presentations in the country of authorisation.  Where there is more than one active substance contained in the medicinal product, data element B.4.k.2.2 'Active substance name(s)' should be repeated accordingly.

f.title: Record therapeutic class only in the narrative and follow up class-only cases
f.statement: Where the product can only be described by therapeutic class, or other therapies cannot be structured, or a food interaction (e.g. grapefruit juice) is reported, the information should only be in the narrative and not in structured product or substance fields. A case suspected to relate only to a therapeutic class is incomplete and does not qualify as an ICSR; efforts should be made to follow up for the missing product information.
f.clause: VI.C.6.2.2.2. Information on suspect, interacting and concomitant medicinal products (c. therapeutic class)
f.applicability: Reports naming only a therapeutic class

rows.quote: Where the medicinal product cannot be described on the basis of the active substances or the invented names, for example when only the therapeutic class is reported by the primary source, or in case of other administered therapies that cannot be structured, this information should only be reflected in the case narrative. The information should not be included in the structured data elements of the medicinal product name or the active substance name(s). The same applies if a suspected food interaction is reported (e.g. to grapefruit juice). Where a case of adverse reactions is suspected to be related only to a therapeutic class, it is considered incomplete and does not qualify for submission as ICSR (see VI.B.2. for ICSRs validation). Efforts should be made to follow-up the case in order to collect the missing information regarding the suspected medicinal product (see VI.B.3. for follow-up guidance).

f.title: Code suspected interactions and mark interacting drugs as 'interacting'

For drug/drug interactions, the drug section (B.4 / G.k) should contain the reported substances/products, with characterisation of drug role (B.4.k.1 / G.k.1) 'interacting' for all suspected interacting medicines. For drug/food or other non-drug interactions, the medicine goes in the drug section and the food/non-drug compound in the narrative.

f.statement: If the primary source suspects a causal role of an excipient, it should be entered as a separate entry in the drug section (E2B(R2) B.4 / E2B(R3) G.k) in addition to the suspected product, and specified in the case narrative. Available positive or negative test results on the excipient's causal role should be included in B.3 / F.r.
f.clause: VI.C.6.2.2.2. Information on suspect, interacting and concomitant medicinal products (e. excipients)

rows.quote: If the primary source suspects a possible causal role of one of the excipients (e.g. colouring matter, preservatives, adjuvant, stabilisers, thickeners, emulsifiers, flavouring and aromatic substances, see VI.A.1.3. for definition) of the suspected medicinal product, this information should be provided in line with ICH-E2B as follows: Reference E2B(R2)/(R3) requirements ICH-E2B(R2)  In the section B.4 ‘Drug information’: as a separate entry specifying the suspected excipient, in addition to the information given regarding the suspected medicinal product. This should also be specified in the case narrative.  If available, tests results (positive or negative) in relation to the causal role of the suspected excipient should be included in the section B.3 'Results of tests and procedures relevant to the investigation of the patient'.

f.title: Capture additional drug information (expiry, batch testing, overdose, misuse, off-label, counterfeit) in E2B
f.statement: Additional characteristics of the medicines pertinent to the case should be captured: in E2B(R2), as free text in B.4.k.19 'Additional information on drug' (also for indications not describable in B.4.k.11), with an appropriate MedDRA term in B.2 and optionally B.5.3/B.5.4; in E2B(R3), coded in G.k.10.r (Counterfeit, Overdose, Drug taken by father, Drug taken beyond expiry date, Batch and lot tested within/not within specifications, Medication error, Misuse, Abuse, Occupational exposure, Off label use) where the primary source made a clear statement, with MedDRA terms in E.i, optional H.3.r/H.4, and free text in G.k.11. Where there is only an indication in the clinical course, the sender may choose G.k.10.r values at its discretion and should follow up the case. The VI.A.1.2 definitions apply.
f.clause: VI.C.6.2.2.2. Information on suspect, interacting and concomitant medicinal products (f. additional information)

The value(s) should be used where the primary source has made a clear statement related to the additional characteristics of the drug.

f.title: Provide all available information on each suspected adverse reaction
f.statement: All available information on the reported suspected adverse reactions shall be provided for each case, e.g. start and end date or duration, seriousness, outcome at last observation, time interval from administration to onset, the reporter's original words, and the country of occurrence.
f.clause: VI.C.6.2.2.3. Suspected adverse reactions

rows.quote: In line with Article 28(3)(j) of the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012, all available information on the reported suspected adverse reactions shall be provided for each individual case. Examples of relevant information include: the start and end date or duration, seriousness, outcome at the time of last observation, time intervals between the suspect medicinal product administration and the start of the reactions, the original reporter’s words or short phrases used to describe the reactions, the country of occurrence of the reactions.
rows.location: VI.C.6.2.2.3. Suspected adverse reactions
rows.review_note: Review: quote extended to the examples listed in the statement. Double-check: confirmed

f.title: Code diagnoses, signs and symptoms with supported MedDRA versions at LLT level
f.statement: Diagnoses and provisional diagnoses with signs and symptoms should be coded with supported MedDRA versions at LLT level per Points to Consider. If a diagnosis is reported with characteristic signs and symptoms, the preferred option is to code the diagnosis only; if no diagnosis is given, all reported signs and symptoms should be coded (the sender may additionally code a diagnosis as sender's diagnosis). Other events in the narrative not typical of the diagnosis and suspected to be adverse reactions should also be listed and coded.
f.clause: VI.C.6.2.2.3. Suspected adverse reactions

rows.quote: In practice, if a diagnosis is reported with characteristic signs and symptoms, the preferred option is to select a term for the diagnosis only and to MedDRA code it. If no diagnosis is provided, all reported signs and symptoms should be listed and MedDRA-coded. If these signs and symptoms are typically part of a diagnosis, the diagnosis can be MedDRA-coded in addition in the ICSR by the competent authority in the Member State or by the marketing authorisation holder as part of the sender's diagnosis and sender’s comment. If in the narrative other events have been reported, which are not typically signs or symptoms of the primary source's diagnosis or provisional diagnosis, and those events are suspected to be adverse reactions, they should also be listed and MedDRA-coded.
rows.location: VI.C.6.2.2.3. Suspected adverse reactions

f.title: Provide alternative or combined diagnosis in sender's diagnosis with reasoning in sender's comments
f.statement: Where the sender disagrees with the primary source diagnosis, an alternative diagnosis can be provided as sender's diagnosis, with reasoning in sender's comments. In this situation, reasoning should be included as sender’s comment

f.title: Provide date and cause of death, including autopsy findings, for fatal cases
f.statement: In the event of the patient's death, the date and cause of death including autopsy-determined causes shall be provided as available, following the EudraVigilance Business Rules and EU ICSR Implementation Guide. If death is unrelated to the suspected reaction (e.g. disease progression), the seriousness criterion should not be considered fatal.
f.clause: VI.C.6.2.2.3. Suspected adverse reactions

rows.quote: In the event of death of the patient, the date, cause of death including autopsy-determined causes shall be provided as available [IR 28 (3) (l)]. The recommendation provided in the EudraVigilance Business Rules54 and the EU Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) Implementation Guide55 should be followed with regard to the provision in the ICSR of information on the patient’s death. If the death is unrelated to the reported suspected adverse reaction(s) and is linked for example to disease progression, the seriousness criterion should not be considered as fatal.
rows.location: VI.C.6.2.2.3. Suspected adverse reactions

f.title: Provide a chronological case narrative for all serious cases, where possible
f.statement: A case narrative shall be provided, where possible, for all cases except non-serious cases, presented in logical time sequence in the chronology of the patient's experience, including clinical course, therapeutic measures, outcome and follow-up information; relevant autopsy or post-mortem findings shall be summarised. The narrative should follow ICH-E2D as a stand-alone medical report (patient characteristics, therapy, history, clinical course, diagnoses, reactions and outcomes, laboratory evidence with normal ranges, supporting/refuting information), be consistent with structured E2B data and be entered in B.5.1 (R2) or H.1 (R3).
f.clause: VI.C.6.2.2.4. Case narrative, comments and causality assessment (a. Case narrative)
f.exceptions: Not required for non-serious cases; 'where possible' means sufficient information received to prepare a concise clinical summary.

rows.quote: In accordance with Article 28 (3)(m) of the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012, a case narrative shall be provided, where possible56, for all cases with the exception of non-serious cases. The information shall be presented in a logical time sequence, in the chronology of the patient’s experience including clinical course, therapeutic measures, outcome and follow-up information obtained. Any relevant autopsy or post-mortem findings shall also be summarised.

f.title: Exclude patient-identifying information from case narratives
f.statement: Patient identifiability information in narratives should follow local data protection laws; narratives should not include information that could identify the patient, including references to healthcare professionals or treatment centres.

f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Data integrity & records

rows.quote: With regard to the identifiability of the patient, information should be provided in accordance with local data protection laws (see VI.C.6.2.2.10. for guidance on the processing of personal data in the EU). Case narratives should not include information that could lead to the identification of the patient, including references to healthcare professionals or treatment centres.

f.title: Provide primary source comments and sender assessment in the comments data elements

f.clause: VI.C.6.2.2.4. Case narrative, comments and causality assessment (b. Comments)

ICH-E2B(R3)  Data element H.2 ‘Reporter's Comments’.

f.title: Sender may add its own assessment, disagreement and emerging-issue summary in Sender’s comments
f.statement: The competent authority or MAH may provide an assessment of the case, describe disagreement with and/or alternatives to the primary source diagnoses, and highlight discrepancies or confusions in the notified information. Where the case leads to notification of an emerging safety issue, a summary of the points of concern and the actions proposed should also be included. This is provided in E2B(R2) B.5.4 or E2B(R3) H.4 ‘Sender’s comments’.
f.clause: VI.C.6.2.2.4. Case narrative, comments and causality assessment (b. Comments)

rows.quote:
The competent authority in a Member State and the marketing authorisation holder may provide an assessment of the case and describe a disagreement with, and/or alternatives to the diagnoses given by the primary source (see VI.C.6.2.2.3. for guidance on the processing of suspected adverse reactions in ICSRs). Discrepancies or confusions in the information notified by the primary source may also be highlighted. Where applicable, a summary of the points of concerns and the actions proposed should also be included in the ICSR when it leads to the notification of an emerging safety issue (see VI.C.2.2.6. for guidance on emerging safety issue). In line with ICH-
E2B this information should be provided in the following data elements: Reference E2B(R2)/(R3) requirements ICH-E2B(R2)  Data element B.5.4 ‘Sender's comments’. ICH-E2B(R3)  Data element H.4 ‘Sender's Comments’.

f.title: Provide structured relatedness for each drug-reaction pair by source and method
f.statement: The degree of suspected relatedness of each product to each reaction can be presented in a structured manner for multiple sources and methods, in E2B(R2) section B.4.k.18 or E2B(R3) section G.k.9.i 'Drug-reaction(s)/Event(s) Matrix', repeated as applicable.
f.clause: VI.C.6.2.2.4. Case narrative, comments and causality assessment (c. Causality assessment)

rows.quote: The degree of suspected relatedness of each medicinal product to each reported adverse reaction can be presented in a structured manner in the ICSR. It can be expressed for multiple sources (reporters, competent authorities, marketing authorisation holders) while using multiple methods of causality assessment. In line with ICH-E2B this information should be provided in the following sections: Reference E2B(R2)/(R3) requirements ICH-E2B(R2)  Section B.4.k.18 ‘Relatedness of drug to reaction(s)/event(s)’. The data elements of this section should be repeated as applicable to provide the assessment of relatedness of each drug-reaction pair expressed by multiple sources and with multiple methods of assessment. ICH-E2B(R3)  Section G.k.9.i ‘Drug-reaction(s)/Event(s) Matrix’. The data elements of this section should be repeated as applicable to provide the assessment of relatedness of each drug-reaction pair expressed by multiple sources and with multiple methods of assessment.

f.title: Provide positive and negative results of relevant tests and procedures
f.statement: Results of tests and procedures relevant to the investigation of the patient shall be provided, including those performed to diagnose or confirm the reaction and to exclude non-drug causes; both positive and negative results should be included. Investigations should be coded per MedDRA Points to Consider, with free text where structuring is impossible: E2B(R2) B.3 (B.3.1 structured, B.3.2 other) or E2B(R3) F.r (test date, name, result, normal low/high, comments; F.r.2.1 free-text name where no MedDRA code; F.r.3.4 unstructured result where no UCUM unit), using a separate block per test.
f.clause: VI.C.6.2.2.5. Test results

rows.quote:
In accordance with the requirements provided in Article 28(3)(k) of the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012, information on the results of tests and procedures relevant to the investigation of the patient shall be provided in the ICSR. This includes tests and procedures performed to diagnose or confirm the reaction/event, including those tests done to investigate (exclude) a non-
drug cause, (e.g. serologic tests for infectious hepatitis in suspected drug-induced hepatitis). Both positive and negative results should be included in the ICSR. The coding of investigations should be performed in line with the latest version of the Guide for MedDRA Users, MedDRA Term Selection: Points to Consider (see GVP Annex IV). If it is not possible to provide information on tests and test results in a structured manner, provisions have been made to allow for the presentation of the information in free text.

f.title: Provide key supplementary record information and flag documents held by sender

E2B(R2) does not support attachments; requested documents should then be sent separately as specified in the request. The processing of personal data should follow local data protection law.
f.clause: VI.C.6.2.2.6. Supplementary records/information

f.statement: Other known case identifiers relevant for duplicate detection should be presented systematically in E2B(R2) section A.1.11 or E2B(R3) section C.1.9.1 'Other case identifiers in previous transmissions'.

ICH-E2B(R3)  Section C.1.9.1 ‘Other case identifiers in previous transmissions’.

f.title: Update date of most recent information on every follow-up and keep initial identifiers and dates unchanged
f.statement: The date of receipt of the most recent information (a precise day-month-year date) should be updated each time follow-up information is received, whether or not it is significant enough to submit. The worldwide unique case identification number of the initial ICSR should be maintained and the date first received from the reporter should remain the date the organisation became aware of the initial report.

f.statement: When an organisation receives follow-up on a case initially submitted to EudraVigilance by another organisation, it should preserve the first organisation's worldwide unique case identification number in subsequent submissions and update the sender's safety report unique identifier and sender identifier with its own.

f.title: Make new follow-up information identifiable in the narrative and complete mandatory follow-up data elements
f.statement: New follow-up information should always be clearly identifiable in the case narrative (required for serious reports) and captured in structured format. For follow-up ICSRs always complete: E2B(R2) A.1.0.1, A.1.6 (unchanged), A.1.7, A.1.10 (unchanged), A.3.1.2 and B.5.1 (serious); E2B(R3) C.1.1, C.1.4 (unchanged), C.1.5, C.1.8 (unchanged), C.3.2 and H.1 (serious).

f.title: Submit follow-up ICSRs for significant new medical information, including downgrades

f.title: Nullify erroneous or duplicate cases following the ICH-E2B nullification principles
f.statement: Nullification should be used where a previously transmitted report is considered completely void (e.g. the whole case is erroneous, or duplicate reports). Principles: the nullification reason should be clear and concise (‘the report no longer meets the criteria for submission’ or ‘report sent previously in error’ are not detailed enough); only the original sending organisation can nullify a case; a nullified case cannot be reactivated; individual versions (follow-ups) cannot be nullified, only the entire case.

rows.quote: In line with ICH-E2B (see GVP Annex IV), the nullification of individual cases should be used to indicate that a previously transmitted report should be considered completely void (nullified), for example when the whole case was found to be erroneous or in case of duplicate reports. The following principles should be followed:  The nullification reason should be clear and concise to explain why this case is no longer considered to be a valid report. For example a nullification reason stating, ‘the report no longer meets the criteria for submission’ or ‘report sent previously in error’ are not detailed enough explanations;  An individual case can only be nullified by the original sending organisation;  Once an individual case has been nullified, the case cannot be reactivated;  Individual versions (i.e. follow-up reports) of a case cannot be nullified, only the entire individual case to which they refer;

f.title: Keep records of literature searches and demonstrate due diligence
f.statement: Records of literature searches should be maintained per IR Art 12, and MAHs should demonstrate due diligence in searching. Good practice is to retain the search construction, database used and date run, and results for an appropriate period, particularly for zero results; documented decision-making on results is particularly important to retain.
f.clause: VI.App.2.4. Record keeping
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Safety intake & collection; Audit & inspection readiness

rows.quote: Records of literature searches should be maintained in accordance with the requirements described in Article 12 of the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012. Marketing authorisation holders should demonstrate due diligence in searching published medical literature. It is always good practice to retain a record of the search construction, the database used and the date the search was run. In addition, it may be useful to retain results of the search for an appropriate period of time, particularly in the event of zero results. If decision making is documented on the results, it is particularly important to retain this information.
rows.location: VI.App.2.4. Record keeping
rows.review_note: Review: confirmed. Double-check: confirmed; quote extended to the zero-results and decision-making sentences.

f.title: Retrieve and review title, citation and abstract for literature search results
f.statement: The title, citation and abstract (if available) of search results should always be retrieved and reviewed.
f.clause: VI.App.2.5. Outputs

rows.quote: Consistent with the requirement to provide the full citation for an article and to identify relevant publications, the title, citation and abstract (if available) should always be retrieved and reviewed.

f.title: Use trained reviewers, record review confirmation and QC literature selection
f.statement: The person reviewing search results is expected to be trained to identify relevant articles (an information professional trained in PV or a PV professional with database knowledge). Recorded confirmation of review helps demonstrate a systematic approach, and quality control checks on a sample of reviews/selections are recommended. Review should also identify relevant studies without ICSRs and non-submittable reports for PSUR production.
f.clause: VI.App.2.6. Review and selection of articles
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Training & competency; ICSR quality control

rows.quote: Therefore, it is expected that the person reviewing the results of a search is trained to identify the articles of relevance. This may be an information professional trained in pharmacovigilance or a pharmacovigilance professional with knowledge of the database used. Recorded confirmation that the search results have been reviewed will assist in demonstrating that there is a systematic approach to collecting information about suspected adverse reactions from literature sources. It is recommended that quality control checks are performed on a sample of literature reviews / selection of articles to check the primary reviewer is identifying the relevant articles.
rows.location: VI.App.2.6. Review and selection of articles

f.title: Obtain likely relevant articles promptly and assume product ownership when unspecified
f.statement: Where outputs may contain a valid ICSR, the article should be ordered; all articles likely relevant to pharmacovigilance should be obtained, with urgency proportionate to the content. Articles may be excluded if another company's branded product is suspected; absent a specified product source or invented name, ownership should be assumed for articles about an active substance.
f.clause: VI.App.2.6. Review and selection of articles

rows.deadline: Urgency proportionate to the content
rows.quote: Outputs from searches may contain enough information to be a valid ICSR, in which case the article should be ordered. All articles for search results that are likely to be relevant to pharmacovigilance requirements should be obtained, as they may contain valid ICSRs or relevant safety information. The urgency with which this occurs should be proportionate to the content of the material reviewed and the resulting requirement for action as applicable for the marketing authorisation holder. Articles can be excluded for the submission of valid ICSRs by the marketing authorisation holder if another company's branded medicinal product is the suspected medicinal product. In the absence of a specified medicinal product source and/or invented name, ownership of the medicinal product should be assumed for articles about an active substance.

rows.review_note: Review: confirmed. Double-check: confirmed; quote extended back to the ordering and urgency sentences.

f.title: Set literature day zero at search date for abstracts and at availability of minimum information for ordered articles
f.statement: Day zero is when the organisation, including any personnel or contracted third party, becomes aware of a publication containing the minimum information. With weekly searching, day zero for a reaction in an abstract is the date the search was conducted; for ordered articles it is the date the minimum information becomes available. Organisations should obtain articles promptly to confirm validity.
f.clause: VI.App.2.7. Day zero

rows.deadline: Day zero = search date (abstract) or date minimum information available (ordered article)
rows.quote: As described in VI.B.7., day zero is the date on which an organisation becomes aware of a publication containing the minimum information for an ICSR to qualify for submission. Awareness of a publication includes any personnel of that organisation, or third parties with contractual arrangements with the organisation. It is sometimes possible to identify the date on which a record was available on a database, although with weekly literature searching, day zero for the submission of an adverse reaction present in an abstract is taken to be the date on which the search was conducted. For articles that have been ordered as a result of literature search results, day zero is the date when the minimum information for an ICSR to be valid is available. Organisations should take appropriate measures to obtain articles promptly in order to confirm the validity of a case.
rows.location: VI.App.2.7. Day zero
rows.review_note: Review: confirmed. Double-check: confirmed; quote extended back to the awareness definition (personnel and contracted third parties).

f.title: Start the clock at the earliest awareness by the MAH or its literature contractor
f.statement: For contracted literature services, the clock starts with awareness of minimum information by the organisation or contractual partner, whichever is earliest; where the third party provides a review or collated report, day zero is the date the search was run if minimum criteria are in the abstract, not the date the information was supplied to the organisation.

f.title: Do not resubmit cases updated only with EudraVigilance master case information
f.statement: It is up to the MAH to decide whether to process EudraVigilance “master cases”.
